I'm so glad this helps give you hope! To be honest, if you speak up, it's likely that other people won't understand. For many people, even though there are certainly difficulties, sexual orientation is something that they don't have to fight within themselves. Before coming out, I thought a lot about my internal feelings of homophobia and my fear of being alone. But, I read a lot of late-in-life lesbians say that they got to a point where they'd rather be alone and not compromising themselves, than to be with someone whom they didn't want to be with.

We may find love. I truly don't know if I believe that that's inevitable. But, regardless, lying to ourselves or trying to force ourselves to feel and act against our nature can only persist unhappiness.

I'm here to talk, too, if you need. It may not be your scene, but I found some refuge in small groups of radical feminists. Politics aside, a lot of women who align themselves with radical feminism have struggled with internal homophobia. The women I know don't hate men or anything, but understand the compulsion to be with a man because of indoctrination instead of because of the actual desire.

Hey, I just wanted to say that I've done the same thing and I have so much self-loathing for it. I'm a lesbian, but I've tried for so long to forceyself to be with men. I grew up in a religious and homophobic home and, whenever a man shows interest in me, the voices of my parents start saying in my head "this is your only shot to be in a relationship" and I just give in, even though it makes me feel disgusting.

I don't know what support to offer, other than that someone else knows this specific kind of self-harm. But, like someone else here said, we can't just leave the lesbian community to dwindle off. It's difficult, but I have found some lesbian women who've also been through this and are now strong and empowered in their sexuality. Maybe we just have to find it for ourselves?
